records.publication: Rowsey et al. (2022), Journal of Mammalogy 103:1259–1277

items.label: Head and ears
items.statement: A long, narrow snout and small eyes and ears form part of the published external diagnosis.
items.limitation: Combination of characters; not a visual confirmation from a distant image.
items.source: Rowsey et al. (2022), Journal of Mammalogy 103:1259–1277

items.label: Coat and tail
items.statement: Dense dark fur covers the body. The visibly haired tail tapers and is shorter than head-and-body length.
items.limitation: Preserved skin and live appearance can differ.
items.source: Rowsey et al. (2022), Journal of Mammalogy 103:1259–1277

items.label: Published body measures
items.statement: The type-series comparison reports head-and-body lengths of 131–143 mm and a tail close to 74% of head-and-body length.
items.limitation: These values describe specimens in the study and are not mandatory cutoffs.
items.source: Rowsey et al. (2022), Journal of Mammalogy 103:1259–1277

items.label: Distinction from Tarsomys and Limnomys
items.statement: The published comparison uses external proportions and cranial traits, not snout shape alone, to distinguish Baletemys from related Philippine shrew-mice.
items.limitation: Skull characters need examination of suitable material; the panel is not a field key.
items.source: Rowsey et al. (2022), Journal of Mammalogy 103:1259–1277

items.label: Observed montane habitat
items.statement: Study specimens came from old-growth montane and mossy forest on Mt. Kampalili at 1,640 and 1,900 m.
items.limitation: Capture heights are observations, not a complete altitudinal range.
items.source: Rowsey et al. (2022), Journal of Mammalogy 103:1259–1277

items.label: Documented collection area
items.statement: The original description documents two collection localities about six kilometres apart on southern Mt. Kampalili, eastern Mindanao.
items.limitation: The authors discuss potential occurrence elsewhere; broader range is not confirmed.
items.source: Rowsey et al. (2022), Journal of Mammalogy 103:1259–1277

records.publication: Herr et al. (2021), Ichthyology & Herpetology 109:197 ff.

items.label: Fanged frog morphology
items.statement: The species has conspicuous sexually dimorphic mandibular odontoid processes typical of Limnonectes.
items.limitation: Shared genus-level characters alone do not separate species.
items.source: Herr et al. (2021), Ichthyology & Herpetology 109:197 ff.

items.label: Advertisement call versus L. acanthi
items.statement: The original treatment distinguishes its single-pulse advertisement notes from the two-pulse notes reported for Palawan-region L. acanthi.
items.limitation: Call comparison assumes good recording and a correct reference population.
items.source: Herr et al. (2021), Ichthyology & Herpetology 109:197 ff.

items.label: Finger and snout comparisons
items.statement: The published comparison with L. diuatus and L. ferneri notes a rounded lateral snout outline and a first finger longer than the second.
items.limitation: Several characters should be considered together; body proportions vary.
items.source: Herr et al. (2021), Ichthyology & Herpetology 109:197 ff.

items.label: Dorsal skin ridges
items.statement: The original treatment describes irregular, broken dorsolateral ridges rather than one continuous ridge.
items.limitation: A wet or partly obscured frog can hide shallow skin relief.
items.source: Herr et al. (2021), Ichthyology & Herpetology 109:197 ff.

items.label: Male holotype length
items.statement: The adult male holotype PNM 9870 measured 74.9 mm in snout–vent length.
items.limitation: A single holotype measurement is not a species-wide size range.
items.source: Herr et al. (2021), Ichthyology & Herpetology 109:197 ff.

items.label: Documented islands
items.statement: The original treatment and the taxonomic catalogue record the species on Mindoro and Semirara.
items.limitation: Historical L. acanthi records from Mindoro require taxonomic reassessment.
items.source: Herr et al. (2021), Ichthyology & Herpetology 109:197 ff.

items.label: Keel of ventral scales
items.statement: The published comparative diagnosis, transcribed in The Reptile Database, describes strongly keeled ventral scales in V. mabitang versus smoother ventrals in V. olivaceus.
items.limitation: Scale texture requires a well-resolved close view or specimen examination.
items.sourceLocation: Reptile Database transcription of original diagnosis

items.label: Dorsal markings
items.statement: Dorsal coloring is predominantly dark with small yellow markings on portions of neck, back and limb scales.
items.limitation: Colour alone is unreliable, especially with dark V. nuchalis on Panay.
items.sourceLocation: Reptile Database transcription of original diagnosis

items.label: Published Panay locality
items.statement: The type locality is near Pandan, Antique, on Panay; the taxonomic catalogue lists Panay.
items.limitation: A type-locality height does not set a geographic or elevational boundary.

items.label: Tree and fruit feeding reports
items.statement: The reptile reference lists tree-associated activity and a predominantly fruit-based diet.
items.limitation: Natural-history generalizations are not a detection or occupancy record.
